chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Shādhān ibn al-Khalīl al-Naysābūrī, from Yūnus, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥusayn, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed wudu (ablution) while wearing a turban, and removing the turban was difficult for him because of the cold. He said: “Let him insert his finger.”

This report indicates that restricting oneself to a single finger in a state of necessity due to cold or other than it is sufficient. It has already preceded that wiping with three fingers is preferable, so there is no basis for repeating it.

As for what Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ẓarīf ibn Nāṣiḥ, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbdillāh, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who wipes his head from behind while he is wearing a turban, with his finger—does that suffice him? He said: “Yes.”

So it does not contradict what we presented earlier, that the wiping ought to be on the front of the head, because it is not impossible for a person to insert his finger from behind and yet wipe with it the front of his head. And it is possible that the report was issued by way of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of some of the ʿĀmmah, and that which confirms what we have mentioned.

key_terms.إِصْبَعَهُ: his finger, used here for wiping
key_terms.مُقَدَّمِ ٱلرَّأْسِ: the front part of the head
key_terms.ٱلتَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation/precaution in expression under certain circumstances
key_terms.ٱلْبَرْدِ: cold, as a circumstance causing hardship
key_terms.ٱلْعِمَامَةِ: the turban worn on the head

ai.seo_question: Does wiping the head with one finger over or under a turban suffice in wudu (ablution) according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal ruling in wudu (ablution) concerning wiping the head while wearing a turban in conditions of hardship such as cold. It indicates that wiping with one finger may suffice in necessity, while also affirming that wiping the front of the head is the preferred rule and noting the possibility of taqiyyah in one report.
